I barely see any hate for Hinglish in India. What I do see hate for is English - proper English. Not some vernacular + English mix. Paternally, I come from a pretty rural family where I was the first person out of almost 30 people who grew up in a large city and could speak crisp, fluent English since my childhood. It's cognitively my primary native language. I have also lived with 1000s of people from both north Indian and south Indian rural areas. How many problems I faced as a result of these differences is something I know. I tend to be very wary of "angreji mat jhaad" batches (including equivalent non-Hindi types). "Angreji mat jhaad" batches often go on their "russia-china-japan-south korea", "colonial mentality", "macaulay", "white bootlicker", "angreji ghulaami ke maansik rogi", "indian culture", "brown sahib", "Hindi medium guy became IIT topper and ISRO scientist", "Bangla medium guy is the best surgeon in our hospital", "japanese are the best and they don't speak English", "english is only a language, not knowledge, not a measure of intelligence", "they only got jobs due to their english, not their skill" rants. They leave their 10 equivalent Hindi YouTube channels that exist and come onto 1 English Indian channel and demand Hindi there. They don't do it on Telugu, Kannada, Tamil etc. channels. It becomes annoying after a while. Bitterness and insecurity start flowing like a fast acting poison through their veins when they see two English fluent Indians converse with each other in a carefree manner. Sometimes they just resort to utterly mannerless behaviour. It is difficult for me to welcome angreji mat jhaad batches into my ecosystem. I tend to keep them out because of repeated experiences with their own behaviour. When their crappy behaviour is called out, they resort to every form of pseudo-victimhood: casteism, "racism", elitism, colonialism....anything except acknowledge their own mindset and improve their English.
